abbott_smith_html:
ἀτιμία, -ας, ἡ
(ἄτιμος) [in LXX for כְּלִמָּה, קָלוֹן, etc. ;]
dishonour, disgrace: 1Co.11:14, 2Co.6:8; εἰς ἀ., Rom.9:21, 2Ti.2:20; ἐν ἀ., 1Co.15:43; κατ᾽ ἀ., 2Co.11:21; πάθη ἀτιμίας, base passions, Rom.1:26.†
(AS)

occurrences.bsb: For this reason God gave them over to dishonorable passions. Even their women exchanged natural relations for unnatural ones.
occurrences.kjv: For this cause God gave them up unto vile affections: for even their women did change the natural use into that which is against nature:

occurrences.bsb: Does not the potter have the right to make from the same lump of clay one vessel for special occasions and another for common use?
occurrences.kjv: Hath not the potter power over the clay, of the same lump to make one vessel unto honour, and another unto dishonour?

occurrences.bsb: Doesn’t nature itself teach you that if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him,
occurrences.kjv: Doth not even nature itself teach you, that, if a man have long hair, it is a shame unto him?

occurrences.bsb: It is sown in dishonor; it is raised in glory. It is sown in weakness; it is raised in power.
occurrences.kjv: It is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power:

occurrences.bsb: through glory and dishonor, slander and praise; viewed as imposters, yet genuine;
occurrences.kjv: By honour and dishonour, by evil report and good report: as deceivers, and yet true;

occurrences.bsb: To my shame I concede that we were too weak for that! Speaking as a fool, however, I can match what anyone else dares to boast about.
occurrences.kjv: I speak as concerning reproach, as though we had been weak. Howbeit whereinsoever any is bold, (I speak foolishly,) I am bold also.

occurrences.bsb: A large house contains not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and clay. Some indeed are for honorable use, but others are for common use.
occurrences.kjv: But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.
